events.title: Louis XVI Is Guillotined
events.description: After being convicted of treason by the National Convention, King Louis XVI of France was executed by guillotine in Paris at age 38.
events.significance: His death ended any hope of a constitutional monarchy in France. It pushed the French Revolution into a more radical phase and alarmed monarchies across Europe.

events.title: Vladimir Lenin Dies
events.description: Lenin, founder of the Soviet state, died at his country estate at Gorki after a series of strokes.
events.significance: His death set off a power struggle that ended with Joseph Stalin in control. It shaped the course of the Soviet Union for decades.

events.title: USS Nautilus Is Launched
events.description: First Lady Mamie Eisenhower launched the USS Nautilus at Groton, Connecticut. It was the world's first nuclear-powered submarine.
events.significance: Nuclear propulsion let submarines stay submerged for long periods. This changed naval strategy and the Cold War balance of power.

events.title: Concorde Begins Passenger Service
events.description: British Airways and Air France began commercial supersonic flights on the same day. One flew from London to Bahrain and the other from Paris to Rio de Janeiro.
events.significance: Concorde cut transatlantic travel times to about three and a half hours. It remains a landmark of aviation engineering.
